thread:
emily: heads-up — i'm preparing a terraform change to tighten the telemetry namespace SA policy in staging. plan: remove the wildcard s3 permissions from the current role and create a scoped role with only the putObject prefix we need. also renaming the irsa annotation to match the new role. ci failed this morning after i tested the tf plan, looks like the role arn changed and the pod can't assume the sa. anyone see any gotchas with doing a canary rollout?

raj: quick q — which annotation key are we standardizing on? our webhook looks for `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` but some old services use `iam.amazonaws.com/role` (yikes).

emily: we're standardizing on `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn`. i'll add a small migration snippet to create a new SA and annotate it, then patch the deployment to use the new SA.

jordan: +1 to new SA approach. to avoid downtime, do this: create new sa with annotation, update deployment to add `spec.template.spec.serviceAccountName: telemetry-uploader-v2`, use `rollingUpdate` with maxUnavailable: 1. once stable, delete old SA. you can also add an annotation on the deployment to force a pod restart: `kubectl patch deploy telemetry -n telemetry --type='strategic' -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"telemetry/sa-migration":"2026-03-10"}}}}}'`.

lina: one heads-up — the uploader also reads a KMS-encrypted secrets file from s3 and the kms policy references the old role arn. you'll need to add the new role to the KMS key policy or rotate the key permissions; otherwise GetObject will fail even if assume-role works.

emily: good catch. i'll update the key policy in the same change set.

raj: terraform diff i ran (trimmed):
```hcl
- resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "telemetry_full" {
-   name = "telemetry-full-access"
-   policy = <<POLICY
-   {"Statement":[{"Action":"s3:*","Resource":"*","Effect":"Allow"}],"Version":"2012-10-17"}
-   POLICY
- }
+ resource "aws_iam_role" "telemetry_uploader_v2" {
+   name = "telemetry-uploader-v2"
+ }
+ resource "aws_iam_policy" "telemetry_putonly" {
+   policy = <<POLICY
+   {"Statement":[{"Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:PutObjectAcl"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::redwood-telemetry-prod/uploads/*"],"Effect":"Allow"}],"Version":"2012-10-17"}
+   POLICY
+ }
+ resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "telemetry_attach" {
+   role = aws_iam_role.telemetry_uploader_v2.name
+   policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.telemetry_putonly.arn
+ }
```

infra-bot: deploy-checker detected failed pods in `staging/telemetry` — 3/5 restarts with `Unauthorized` on s3 GetObject (role mis-match). :warning:

jordan: for the tf plan, consider adding a `depends_on` between the role creation and the deployment patch so rollout only starts after role + policy + kms policy update are applied. also add a `null_resource` local-exec that runs `kubectl apply -f` for the SA so TF orchestrates the order.

lina: also consider creating a short-lived compatibility role binding: give the old role assume-role permission to the new role (sts:AssumeRole) as a fallback for 24-48h, then remove it after monitoring. keeps things safe for client pods that haven't restarted.

emily: good idea, i'll add a temporary trust relationship and a note in the PR.

raj: one more nit — our admission webhook rejects SA annotations if namespace label `redwood/managed-by` != `platform`. telemetry namespace is `platform-managed` currently, so the webhook stripped the annotation when i tried to apply the new SA in staging. need to either update the namespace label or adjust the webhook exception.

emily: ugh, that's why the SA didn't get the annotation. i'll update namespace label in the same PR and call out the webhook change.

jordan: ping me on the PR when it's ready, i'll run the smoke test in staging and validate the uploader logs. suggest leaving a quick eval prompt in console to check token identity: run inside pod `curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/identity-credentials` or `aws sts get-caller-identity` if awscli present.

emily: thanks all — i'll open PR with: role+policy, kms policy update, new SA manifest, namespace label change, deployment patch, and a temporary trust-entry for fallback. will mark the PR with `infra/canary` and link a runbook snippet. expect the PR in ~2h. :seedling:

infra-bot: PR created — #4921 — emily/sa-policy-slimdown. automation ran `terraform plan` and `k8s-validate` (webhook check failed as expected, waiting on namespace label change).

lina: acked and added to my watchlist. i'll hold off on deleting old role until metrics look good for 48h.

emily: updating here if anything unexpected pops up. thanks! :white_check_mark:
